message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key traffic laws and regulations that apply in Texas, along with some practical tips and resources for staying compliant.

---

## 1. Governing Authority

| Agency | Role |
|--------|------|
| **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** | Issues driver’s licenses, vehicle registrations, and enforces state traffic laws. |
| **Texas Transportation Code** | Codified statutes that govern all aspects of driving, vehicle operation, and road safety. |
| **Local Municipalities & County Road Departments** | Enforce local ordinances (e.g., parking restrictions, speed limits on city streets). |

---

## 2. Core Traffic Laws

| Category | Key Statutes / Provisions | Typical Penalties |
|----------|---------------------------|-------------------|
| **Speed Limits** | §545.001 – 545.004 | Fines, points, possible license suspension. |
| **Seat‑belt Use** | §545.021 | $50–$100 fine; points. |
| **Child Restraint** | §545.022 | $50–$200 fine; points. |
| **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | §545.041 – 545.045 | Up to $1,000 fine, license revocation, mandatory alcohol‑abuse treatment. |
| **Cell‑Phone Use** | §545.023 | $50–$200 fine; points. |
| **Right‑of‑Way / Yielding** | §545.011 – 545.013 | Fines, points. |
| **Parking Regulations** | §545.014 – 545.016 | $50–$200 fine; towing. |
| **Traffic Signal Violations** | §545.015 | $50–$200 fine; points. |
| **Reckless Driving** | §545.046 | Up to $1,000 fine, license revocation, possible jail time. |
| **Vehicle Equipment** | §545.020 | Fines for non‑compliant equipment (e.g., broken taillights). |

> **Points System** – Texas uses a point system for most moving‑vehicle violations. Accumulating 12 or more points within 36 months can lead to license suspension.

---

## 3. Common Violations & How to Avoid Them

| Violation | Why It Happens | Prevention Tips |
|-----------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Speeding** | Driver overestimates safe speed or ignores posted limits. | Always obey posted signs; use cruise control on highways. |
| **Seat‑belt/Child Restraint** | Forgetting to buckle up or using improper restraints. | Check seat‑belt status before starting the engine; use approved child seats. |
| **Cell‑Phone Distraction** | Texting or calling while driving. | Use hands‑free devices; pull over if you need to make a call. |
| **Running Red Lights** | Misreading signals or rushing. | Treat all stop signs and red lights as “stop” regardless of traffic flow. |
| **DUI** | Alcohol or drug impairment. | Never drive after drinking; use rideshare or designated driver. |
| **Parking Violations** | Parking in no‑parking zones or blocking driveways. | Read signage; park in designated spots. |

---

## 4. Enforcement & Penalties

| Offense | Fine Range | Points | Additional Consequences |
|---------|------------|--------|------------------------|
| Speeding (up to 20 mph over limit) | $50–$200 | 1–2 | Possible license suspension if repeated. |
| Seat‑belt/Child Restraint | $50–$200 | 1 | |
| DUI (first offense) | $500–$1,000 | 4 | License revocation, mandatory treatment. |
| Cell‑Phone Use | $50–$200 | 1 | |
| Reckless Driving | $500–$1,000 | 4 | Possible jail time. |

> **Note:** Fines can increase if the violation occurs in a school zone, construction zone, or during a traffic accident.

---

## 5. Special Situations

| Situation | Relevant Law | Key Points |
|-----------|--------------|------------|
| **School Bus Stop** | §545.012 | Must stop 20 ft behind bus; failure = $200 fine. |
| **Construction Zones** | §545.012 | Speed limits may be reduced; fines for non‑compliance. |
| **High‑way Interchanges** | §545.001 | Use turn lanes; failure to yield can result in points. |
| **Commercial Vehicles** | §545.030 | Additional equipment requirements (e.g., reflective markings). |

---

## 6. Resources & Where to Get More Information

| Resource | What It Offers |
|----------|----------------|
| **Texas DPS Website** | License renewal, vehicle registration, traffic law updates. |
| **Texas Transportation Code** | Full statutory text (available online). |
| **Texas Highway Patrol** | Enforcement news, safety campaigns. |
| **Local City/County Ordinances** | Specific parking and speed limit rules. |
| **Legal Aid & DUI Defense Services** | If you’re facing charges. |

---

## 7. Quick Reference Cheat Sheet

| Law | Penalty | How to Avoid |
|-----|---------|--------------|
| Speeding | $50–$200 + 1–2 pts | Observe posted limits |
| Seat‑belt | $50–$200 + 1 pt | Buckle before moving |
| Child Restraint | $50–$200 + 1 pt | Use approved seat |
| Cell‑Phone | $50–$200 + 1 pt | Hands‑free or pull over |
| DUI | $500–$1,000 + 4 pts | Don’t drive after drinking |
| Reckless | $500–$1,000 + 4 pts | Drive responsibly |

---

### Bottom Line

Texas traffic laws are designed to protect everyone on the road. By staying aware of the key statutes, keeping your vehicle in good condition, and practicing safe driving habits, you can avoid most common violations and keep your license in good standing. If you ever have a specific question—such as how a particular ordinance applies to your situation—consult the Texas DPS or a qualified attorney.
